title: Rapid Sellcraft: Field Lab Deck (Draft)
summary: A compact, modular slide skeleton + speaker notes for SEs to run a 20–45 minute field-lab with customers. Focus: rapid pilots that test latency/cost tradeoffs, fallback economics, and reserved capacity negotiation signals.
body:
Purpose and audience:
- Quick experiment kit for SEs and Solutions Engineers to run live customer conversations (pilot, integration architect, platform eng).
- Not a polished deck — intentionally modular: pick 6–10 slides for a 20–45m session.

Slide map (pick per call):
1) Title + micro-ask (30s): what we want by end (pilot decision / POC scope / perf goal)
2) Hypothesis framing (60s): "We can improve throughput or cut cost X% while keeping p95 latency <= Yms"
3) Real-world ask (90s): show customer example request, TL;DR of the workload (seq len, concurrency, burst profile)
4) Quick anatomy of serving (90s): cache, batching, kernel variant, routing policy — one-liner per building block
5) Fallback story + economics (3 slides; 3 mins): if capacity constrained -> model variant + routing -> cost delta table + UX tradeoffs
6) Pilot options (2 slides; 2 mins): hosted quick-start vs dedicated reserve vs private on-prem checklist
7) Canary & rollback guardrails (2 slides; 3 mins): canary % ramps, guardrail metrics (latency P95, error rate, token cost diffs)
8) Experiment plan & success metrics (3 slides; 3 mins): sample A/B, sample prompt-set, pass/fail thresholds
9) Next steps checklist (1 slide): who, when, resources needed

Speaker notes excerpts (for SEs):
- Opening: "We usually split risk into two buckets: latency risk (user-visible) and economic risk (per-token cost). Today we’ll map both to a small pilot so you can validate quickly."
- When customer asks about quantization quality: "We run short prompt-set evals (20–50 examples) with your prompts — we measure top-line task metrics + a human spot-check. Quantization often saves 1.5–3x cost at small quality deltas; we make it explicit in the pilot."
- If they worry about fallback complexity: "We recommend deterministic routing policy: region -> model family -> lower-cost variant. The platform handles model mapping — you only define SLO tiers."

Field-lab playlets (roleplay scripts):
- SE script A (integration architect skeptical):
  - Q: "How do you keep user experience stable if I switch model variants?"
  - A: "Auto-fallback pairs the same prompt pipeline and preserves deterministic outputs where possible; we surface regression alerts against your eval set and let you opt into rollbacks instantly."

- SE script B (procurement/time-to-value):
  - Q: "Can you guarantee cost predictability during pilot?"
  - A: "We offer a capped pilot budget + token-alerting and a small reserved-burst buffer; if you want predictable month-over-month, dedicated reservations are the next step."

Micro-metrics to track in pilot (quick glossary):
- TTV: time-to-value (days until integrated demo with real request samples)
- P95-latency (ms): user-facing latency metric (critical for conversational UI)
- Token-cost-delta per 1k: estimated cost change compared to baseline model
- Failure surfaced rate: % requests with fallback activated
- Human-diff-rate: fraction of outputs flagged by human review as degradations

Example quick-econ table (one slide text):
- Baseline model: p95=430ms, cost= $0.44 /k tokens
- Quantized variant: p95=370ms, cost= $0.15 /k tokens, human-diff-rate= 3% on eval set
- Fallback plan: route 85% to quantized, 15% to baseline under high-loss cases -> expected cost = $0.20 /k tokens

Pilot experiment template (copyable into Jira):
- Title: Field-lab pilot: Summarization throughput test
- Duration: 2 weeks (incl. eval)
- Data: 500 representative requests from production / sample dataset
- Success criteria: p95 <= 350ms AND human-diff-rate <= 5% AND token-cost-delta <= 40%
- Rollback trigger: human-diff-rate > 8% OR p95 increase > 15% relative to baseline

Operational guardrails for sellers to promise (short):
- We will surface daily summary: p95, cost per 1k tokens, fallback rate, and top 10 prompts with regressions.
- SEs: configure 1 canonical eval set and 1 holdout set; platform will run nightly scoring.

Negotiation signals & talking points (for AE):
- If they ask for discount on Dedicated: point to observed runway from pilot (TTV and cost delta) + commit to scale rules.
- If compliance is main blocker: emphasize Private option + audit log retention + KMS/HSM integration checklist.

Outstanding questions / data needs (notes to self):
- Get sample of worst-case long sequence call patterns from customer (Jira GTMP-1283)
- Confirm whether customer needs on-prem package for EU data residency
- Add slide that lists exact Confluence playbook snippets for SLO configs

Quick checklist before running a live field-lab call:
- [ ] Load 20–50 sample prompts into eval runner
- [ ] Flag integrator + platform contact and confirm region
- [ ] Attach cost estimate and budget cap in pilot doc (pilot budget alert)
- [ ] Create Jira pilot ticket and link canary config

Version notes and iteration plan:
- v0.1 (this draft): compact script and playlets for SEs
- v0.2: add 2-page quick-eval template + slide with step-by-step console screenshots
- v0.3: curated prompt-sets by vertical (support, summarization, search)

Notes to self: keep language soft-sales, very technical-first. This deck should be used live, not sent as a full polished deck initially.

References / quick links:
- Confluence: INF-Field-Lab-Framework (linked)
- Jira: GTMP-1283 (pilot request backlog)
- GitHub: rapid-sim-playbooks/pull/42 (sim harness for cost calc)

Next steps (ownerable):
- Ethan: fold in console screenshots (by 2025-11-28)
- Priya: vet the quick-eval metrics with Applied ML (by 2025-11-25)
- Liam: produce sample prompt-sets for 3 verticals (by 2025-12-02)

End of draft.

(Notes: intentionally concise — this is a field-first toolkit, not marketing collateral.)
